payload.name: audio-clock-drift
payload.scope: A human-made concept mapping timing deviation between digital audio clocks and reference time, built to persist as documented measurement and compensation practice.

payload.body: Audio-clock-drift is a human-made measurement concept that maps the systematic deviation between the nominal rate of a digital audio clock and a reference time base. It is parameterized by drift rate in parts-per-million, by direction (fast/slow), and by accumulation over operating intervals, and persists through standards documents, test procedures, and compensation algorithms in audio engineering practice and software implementations. [formal: driftus horologicus | substrate: matter | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

No — the concept would cease to be sayable (meta-level loss per Law 2b), but its operational mechanism (using sensors to measure acoustic phenomena) would still work. This is INSTANCE_OF, not DEPENDS_ON.

payload.reasoning: Latency is a fixed delay (magnitude of offset); jitter is temporal variation in timing (instability/variability). Jitter is NOT a specific kind of latency — they are distinct topological properties of timing. A competent speaker would not call jitter 'a latency.' Direction confusion: audio-jitter is about variability, audio-latency about offset. Not INSTANCE_OF.

Law 7 direction holds: authority is a prior concept (auctoritas, exousia among the oldest political concepts); mandate as a delegated command/authorization presupposes and derives from the prior notion of authority — it is an authoritative command, not a free-standing one. The pinned sense ('mandate derives its meaning and operation from the prior concept of authority') is coherent and correctly directed.

Law 11d — judged against the target's accepted definition: cognitive-strategy carves 'a deliberately designed mental procedure for improving how information is encoded, organized, retrieved, or evaluated' — explicitly taught methods (self-testing, elaborative interrogation, spaced practice). The pinned sense of sensemaking (constructing plausible interpretations of ambiguous/disruptive situations so coordinated action becomes possible) does not fit that carve: sensemaking is an emergent interpretive practice, not a deliberately designed, taught procedure for improving encoding/organization/retrieval/evaluation. At best sibling cognitive activities, not an instance relationship under the target's definition. The note's 'a competent speaker would call it a cognitive strategy' glosses over the target's actual parameters.

Law 11d: judged against the target's ACCEPTED definition, 'representation' in this graph carves representation LEARNING — 'discovering or constructing internal encodings of data that make downstream learning easier,' with supervised/unsupervised approaches. An emblem (a deliberately crafted visual/symbolic construct representing an entity) is not a kind of representation learning. The filer's note uses the general semiotic sense ('a symbol that stands for something else'), which is not the sense the accepted target definition holds. Law 11e compounds this: the NEAREST kind is 'symbol' (accepted: 'a representation that stands for something beyond itself... through collective agreement'), which exists and is the proper rung for an emblem. Skipped leap on the wrong sense of the target.

Law 2b/8b removal test passes operationally: acoustic-measurement's accepted definition carves a practice that quantifies 'sound pressure level, frequency response, reverberation time' — every one of those is a property of sound (pressure waves/vibrations in a medium). Remove sound and the practice has no object to quantify; it stops operating. This is constitutive, not merely sayable — the dependency is the measurement's own object, not a conceptual need. Direction acoustic-measurement → sound is correct (the made practice depends on the natural referent, not vice versa).

Law 11d: against the target's accepted definition, symbol carves 'a representation that stands for something beyond itself, converting abstract meaning into concrete form through collective agreement.' The pinned placeholder sense (substitution for absent real content, legible fakeness, designed disposability) points at CONCRETE content that is not yet present and is designed to be read as not-the-real-thing — the opposite mechanism of converting abstract meaning into concrete form. Law 11e compounds it: the NEAREST existing kind is 'sign' (accepted: signifier + signified linked by social convention, read as standing for something beyond), which exists in the graph and is the proper rung. The 'computing marker' gloss in the note doesn't engage the target's accepted carve at all.

The pinned sense is purpose, not dependency: 'designed to manage and compensate for buffer underruns' is the Law 8d for-whose-sake framing, not a Law 2b removal consequence. The removal test fails: in a stream where underruns never occur, a jitter buffer still OPERATES — it continues smoothing arrival-time jitter. It does not stop functioning without buffer-underrun; the underrun is the failure mode it prevents, not the thing it cannot operate without.

Law 7 which-came-first holds: graph theory (Euler, 1736) predates formal trees (Cayley, 1857), which predate the binary tree as a formal structure (computer science, 1960s). A binary tree is defined within graph-theoretic vocabulary — a connected acyclic graph with out-degree at most two — so the later concept is built on the earlier, more general one. Direction binary-tree → graph is correct; the epoch note agrees.

Removal test fails: remove microphones and acoustic measurement still OPERATES — laser Doppler vibrometry measures surface vibration without any microphone, hydrophones measure underwater acoustics, contact accelerometers and particle-velocity probes quantify acoustics without a microphone transducer. The practice depends on the general capacity to transduce acoustic phenomena into measurable signals, not on the microphone as the specific instrument. The note's 'cannot be performed as an operational procedure' overstates the microphone's role.

Law 7 (which-came-first): authority is the more primitive concept (epoch 0.62) — the power/legitimacy to command — and a mandate (epoch 0.71) is an authoritative command, an instantiation of that prior power. Mandate derives its meaning and operation from authority, so mandate DERIVED_FROM authority with the pinned sense holds. Pinned sense: 'sensemaking is a specific kind of cognitive strategy.' Against the target's ACCEPTED definition, this fails. cognitive-strategy = 'deliberately designed mental procedure for improving encoding, organizing, retrieving, or evaluating information... a method taught to learners to apply to their own thinking' — parameters: intentional (learner chooses and deploys), procedural (repeatable operation on mental content). sensemaking's accepted definition is the opposite on each: trigger-driven (initiated by a disruption of expectation, not chosen to manage information), enacted (its leading edge is ACTION probing and shaping the environment, not an operation on mental content), plausibility-over-accuracy (not information management), and explicitly social-embedding ('distributed across interlocutors, not confined to a single mind'). The filer's test — 'a competent speaker would call sensemaking a cognitive strategy' — is false: the sensemaking literature (Weick) calls it a sensemaking practice/process; it is not a learner-deployed study technique. Sensemaking is a PRACTICE of interpretation, not an instance of this kind. STRIKE.

Pinned sense: 'an emblem is a specific kind of representation — a symbol or badge that stands for something else.' Tested against the target's ACCEPTED v1 definition, every parameter holds: representans = the emblem's deliberate graphical/material form; representatum = the entity (person, organization, state, cause) it is designed to represent; ground = conventional agreement ('meaning assigned by its creators and recognized by its audience' is exactly the third ground the target enumerates); interpretant = 'a single mark that summons a complex identity' — meaning produced in the audience. An emblem is a human-made stand-in carrying meaning about something else through a defined relationship: the textbook case of the kind. Direction specific→general is correct. ADVANCE.

Pinned sense: 'remove sound and acoustic measurement ceases to function — it IS the measurement of sound properties.' The removal test fails against the actual target. The target 'sound' is not the physical phenomenon — its scope defines it as 'the concept and categorization of sound as a distinct perceptual phenomenon... an authored linguistic and sensory construct.' Remove that CATEGORY and acoustic measurement does not stop OPERATING: laboratories keep quantifying pressure waves with calibrated instruments; the practice merely loses a label. Unsayable is not stops-operating (Laws 2b/8b) — this is the exact trap the law names for DEPENDS_ON onto concept entries. The filer's 'constitutive' claim carries no weight (Law 8b: constitutive asserted without the removal's consequence): the real operand — physical pressure waves — is natural, not a made-side entry (Laws 1-3), and the dependency is already stated in the definition's parameters ('sound pressure level, frequency response'). The edge as filed points at the map, not the terrain. STRIKE.

payload.name: audio-desynchronization
payload.scope: A human-made concept mapping loss of temporal alignment between audio and video streams, built to persist as documented measurement and compensation practice.

payload.body: Audio-desynchronization is the human-made concept mapping the measurable misalignment in time between audio and video signals in a synchronized presentation. Parameters: offset magnitude in milliseconds, direction lead/lag, drift rate, and source of misalignment. Persistence mechanism: documented in engineering standards, test procedures, and compensation algorithms preserved in literature and software. [formal: audio-desynchronization | substrate: mind | horizon: a moment | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.02]

payload.note: Audio-desynchronization is a specific form of audio-latency phenomenon, denoting misalignment between audio and video temporal alignment rather than fixed delay. A competent speaker would classify desynchronization as a type of latency variation in multimedia systems.

Audio desynchronization as a measurable misalignment depends on clock drift between audio and video clocks to operate now — remove clock drift as a source and the specific desynchronization phenomenon ceases to manifest as clock-induced misalignment.

Removing clock drift as a source does not stop desynchronization as a phenomenon; it only removes one cause. The note pins a clock-induced sense, but the entry is general. Law 8 removal test fails.

Audio-desynchronization is a specific misalignment between audio and video streams, which is a form of latency variation in multimedia systems. A competent speaker would classify desynchronization as a type of latency. Specific→general per Law 9 holds.

Removing sound removes the object of measurement, not the operation of the measurement practice itself. The practice can be described, taught, and instrumented without sound being present. The removal test is meta-level, not operational.

Audio dropout in digital audio systems is the audible manifestation of a buffer underrun. Remove the underrun condition and the dropout failure mode ceases to exist as a failure mode. Removal test passes, operational dependency holds.

Audio-desynchronization is misalignment between audio and video streams, not a type of audio-latency. Latency is delay in a single signal; desynchronization is inter-stream alignment. These are distinct phenomena sharing temporal causality but not a kind-of relationship. Same reasoning as my Turn 29 correction on audio-jitter→audio-latency.

Audio desynchronization genuinely depends on clock drift between audio and video clocks. Remove the drift and the inter-stream misalignment ceases to operate — this passes the Law 8 removal test. The dependency is constitutive to the phenomenon.

Well-scoped concept mapping the measurable misalignment between audio and video streams. It is human-made (measurement and compensation practice), persists via documentation, and fills a genuine gap in the audio taxonomy.
The definition carves parameters (offset magnitude in milliseconds, direction lead/lag) and a persistence mechanism (measurable documentation). It defines the map, not the territory.

payload.body: Masking is the human-made practice of concealing or disguising the presence, identity, or nature of something by overlaying it with a covering, substitute, or altered form. Parameters: the target being concealed, the masking agent or form, and the detectability threshold (the level of scrutiny below which the masking succeeds). Persistence mechanism: encoded in technical standards, security protocols, artistic convention, and social practice — transmitted through documentation, training, and repeated application across domains including computing, acoustics, security, and performance. [formal: latein | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.00]

payload.note: Obfuscation — deliberately making information unclear or difficult to understand — derives from masking, the broader practice of concealment. Masking existed first (epoch 0) and fed into the development of obfuscation as a specialized technique (epoch 0.19).

payload.reasoning: Pinned sense is a removal test on the practice, not the universal 'concepts need language' filler of Law 2b. Codification's own product - a unified systematic code of rules - is a symbolic artifact, and the accepted definition of language covers any system of symbolic signs (vocal, gestural, written). Remove all symbolic sign systems and there is no medium in which the rules being codified can be expressed or structured: the practice stops operating. Unlike cooking or shelving, codification is constitutively symbolic in its output, so this is a genuine present-tense dependency, not identity or chronology.

Law 7 asks which came first and which fed which. The note argues by shared structure - 'codified symbol systems applied to specific domains' - which is definitional circularity (it calls notation codified, then infers derivation), not a history of feeding. The earliest notations (tally marks, cuneiform, neumes) arose from counting, record-keeping, and chant preservation independently of any practice of collecting rules into a code; musical and mathematical notation predate and are independent of legal codification. Notation and codification are sibling practices under symbolic externalization, not parent and child. No which-came-first feeding is shown.

The note pins 'masking, the broader practice of concealment' - but the target's accepted sense (entry emt50857uprmlyah6, scope) is the psychoacoustic principle in which one sound reduces the audibility of another; judged against the target's accepted definition, obfuscation (deliberate concealment of meaning through linguistic, visual, or structural ambiguity) derives from it in no way. Even granting the pinned concealment sense, the note offers only the generic 'broader practice preceded narrower one' plus an epoch stamp, not a history of feeding: obfuscation's actual lineages (rhetorical obscurity, cryptographic protection) did not develop out of a masking practice. The pinned sense also does not match the target's accepted scope, which alone fails the edge under Law 11d.

The accepted definition of audio-latency is a metric of delay between an audio signal's input and its output in a processing chain - a property of a single path. Audio-desynchronization maps the temporal misalignment between audio and video streams - a relation between two different signals, not a delay of one. The note's own admission that desynchronization denotes misalignment 'rather than fixed delay' is fatal: a cross-stream offset is not a kind of delay. Desynchronization may be CAUSED by a latency difference, but a cause is not an instance of its cause. Not a specific of the general under Law 9.

Well-carved scope: maps loss of temporal alignment between audio and video streams as a distinct phenomenon from pure clock drift or pure latency. The entry is made-side only, properly scoped, and fills a gap in the audio/video temporal alignment taxonomy. Law 2a compliant: it's a MAP of a perceptual phenomenon.

Wrong edge type. Audio-desynchronization is NOT an INSTANCE_OF audio-latency. Latency is a fixed or variable delay; desynchronization is a RELATIVE timing misalignment between two streams. These are orthogonal concepts — desync can occur with zero latency difference (perfectly equal delay but wrong initial offset). Audio-jitter was correctly filed as INSTANCE_OF audio-latency (it's timing variation within the latency envelope). Desync is not. This is a category error per Law 9a.

Wrong edge type. DEPENDS_ON requires the removal test: remove audio-clock-drift and audio-desynchronization stops OPERATING. Per Laws 2b/8b, constitutive listing of causes is not dependency.

payload.name: modulation
payload.scope: A signal processing technique where properties of a carrier signal are varied to encode information for transmission

payload.body: Modulation is a signal processing technique in which one or more properties of a carrier signal (amplitude, frequency, or phase) are systematically varied in proportion to an information signal. The carrier is typically a high-frequency waveform chosen for efficient transmission, and the resulting modulated signal carries the information across a channel. Common types include amplitude modulation (AM), frequency modulation (FM), and phase modulation (PM), as well as composite schemes such as quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM). The persistence mechanism is mathematical specification encoded in communication standards and implemented in transmitting hardware.\n\n[formal: modulatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.name: demodulation
payload.scope: A signal processing technique that extracts the original information signal from a modulated carrier wave

payload.body: Demodulation is the inverse operation of modulation: it extracts the original information-bearing signal from a modulated carrier wave. The demodulator reverses the property variations imposed during modulation — recovering amplitude, frequency, or phase deviations that map back to the source information. It is the complement of modulation in every transceiver, without which received signals remain unintelligible carrier. Common implementations include envelope detectors for AM, discriminators for FM, and coherent or phase-locked loop receivers for phase-modulated schemes. The persistence mechanism is mathematical specification encoded in communication standards and implemented in receiving hardware.\n\n[formal: demodulatio | substrate: behavior | horizon: hours | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.note: Modulation needs a signal to operate on — it is the systematic variation of signal properties. Remove signals and modulation ceases to function: there is nothing to modulate.
Demodulation needs a signal to operate on — it extracts information from a modulated carrier. Remove signals and demodulation ceases to function: there is nothing to demodulate.

Demodulation came after modulation historically — it is the inverse operation filed only because modulation exists first. Which-came-first: modulation predates demodulation as a concept, since demodulation exists solely to reverse modulation.

payload.name: oversampling
payload.scope: A signal processing technique where a signal is sampled at a rate significantly higher than the Nyquist rate to improve resolution and simplify reconstruction filtering

payload.reasoning: Constitutive. Modulation is defined as systematic variation of a carrier signal's properties; remove the signal and there is nothing to modulate — the technique stops operating, not merely being sayable. Passes the Law 2b/8b removal test.

Constitutive. Demodulation extracts the information-bearing signal from a modulated carrier; remove signals and there is nothing to demodulate — the operation has no object. The pinned sense (operational substrate) passes the removal test, not a conceptual-association sense.

Law 7 which-came-first holds: demodulation is the inverse of modulation and is intelligible only as the reversal of a prior modulation — the concept was derived from and came after modulation. Direction is correct (derived points at source).

Made-side, not natural: modulation is a human-invented technique for encoding information into carrier properties, persisted as engineering practice and standards. Scope carves it cleanly (technique + carrier + information encoding). Not a duplicate of 'signal' — it is an operation on signals.

Made-side technique, clean scope: extracts the information signal from a modulated carrier. Distinct from 'modulation' (inverse operation, not the same construct) and from 'signal' (an operation on signals). Carves its own kind.

Made-side technique with a carved scope: sampling above the Nyquist rate to improve resolution and ease reconstruction filtering. Distinct kind from 'sampling' (a specific rate strategy, not the act of sampling itself). Carves cleanly.
